body:
## What to build

Expand the stock shelf (SPEC §42: event, note, person, post) into an interconnected standard library — 'the stock graph'. The working spec is `.adlc/specs/49-stock-graph.md`; its acceptance criteria are the rail list. Myk settled the design in chat on 2026-08-25. The settled decisions:

1. CONVERGENCE IS THE GOAL. The shelf becomes a shared vocabulary in anticipation of federation. Two stores that install the same stock shapes share the same `schema:<Name>@<hash>` snapshots, so they provably share readings.
2. THE CATALOG (base props flat, edges annotated with the reading they expand):
   - person (hub): name, bio, email; deep reading expands follows* → ShallowPerson, memberOf* → ShallowOrg
   - place (leaf): name, address, lat, lon
   - attachment (leaf): name, mimeType, size, bytes
   - note (leaf, existing): title, body, tags*
   - bookmark (leaf): url, title, description, tags*
   - org: name, description, website, members* → ShallowPerson
   - event (existing, grows): title, startsAt, endsAt, notes, attending* → ShallowPerson, place → place
   - post (existing, grows): title, body, publishedAt, tags*, mentions* → ShallowPerson, replyTo → post, thread → thread
   - message: body, sentAt, to* → ShallowPerson, replyTo → message, thread → thread
   - thread: title, participants* → ShallowPerson; read through two lenses, PostThread and MessageThread (separate gather programs over the same anchor entities — an expand names ONE reading, so the two nestings are two programs)
   - task: title, status, dueAt, assignedTo → ShallowPerson, tags*
   - document: title, body, status, tags*, attachments* → attachment
   - comment: body, publishedAt, on → ShallowReference (any kind)
   - collection: title, items* → ShallowReference (any kind, curator-signed)
   - ShallowReference: universal reading, resolves any entity to { id }
   - ShallowPerson: id, name. ShallowOrg: id, name.
3. DEPTH IS DECLARED PER EDGE. rhizomatic requires every expand to name its child reading. Shelf rule: deep programs expand with SHALLOW readings, so recursion terminates by construction. Shallow programs expand nothing. `fix` stays off the shelf.
4. DEPENDENCIES ARE DERIVED, NEVER DECLARED. Walk each hyperschema body; collect expand readings (and fix invocations, which the shelf must not have). No hand-written requires list. A rail asserts shelf closure: every reading a shelf body names is itself on the shelf.
5. TRANSITIVE INSTALL. `loam register --stock org` registers org plus every missing dependency, dependency order, leaves first. Each registration is the same verbatim-file path through parseRegistrationInput and publishRegistration (§42.1 invariant holds: --stock changes only how the JSON is obtained). A name already bound is SKIPPED and reported.
6. DIVERGENCE COMPOSES AND WARNS (Myk). If a required name is bound to a non-stock reading (snapshot hash differs from stock), install composes with it and prints one warning line naming the stock hash. Never refuse. Exit 0.
7. RE-RUN IS EVOLVE-WITH-REPORT (Myk). `--stock person` over an older stock person takes the ordinary evolve path and reports it.
8. THE PROP LISTS ARE PINNED (Myk — reverses §42.5). A rail asserts the exact prop list and edge-reading assignment of every shelf entry. Editorial change becomes a deliberate act, because every edit moves the convergence hash. The landing spec section states the reversal.
9. NO CLAIMED IDENTITY FIELDS, shelf-wide doctrine (promoted from post's absent author): no shape carries author/from/creator/sender. The delta signer is the identity. message has to* (recipients), post has mentions*; these are different speech acts and stay distinct roles.
10. replyTo AND thread ARE BOTH PRESENT and orthogonal (the email precedent: In-Reply-To vs References). replyTo gives the tree; thread gives the whole conversation in one gather at the anchor.
11. THREAD MEMBERSHIP IS MEMBER-SIGNED (each message/post points at the anchor; moderation is negation). COLLECTION MEMBERSHIP IS CURATOR-SIGNED (the curator claims items). This governance difference is why thread is not a collection, and the spec teaches it.
12. BUILD AS A STACK of small PRs: machinery first (dependency walk, transitive install, skip-if-bound, divergence warning, pin rail), then shapes leaves-first. Design is one working spec; landing is staged.

## User stories (approved by Myk, 2026-08-25)

1. Sam runs `loam register --stock org`. The CLI reports it also installed shallow-person and person. Sam adds person:ada as a member. A GraphQL org query returns ada's id and name nested — and not ada's follows.
2. Ada replies to a post. Her reply carries replyTo (parent) and thread (anchor). A thread query returns every post in the conversation in one read, no tree walk.
3. Priya already has her own bespoke Person. She runs `--stock org`. The install composes with her Person and warns it is not stock Person@<hash>.
4. Two stores each ran stock. They federate. One person entity, claimed in both stores, appears in both stores' org views under the same reading.
5. The operator strikes a stranger's message from a thread. The thread view no longer shows it; the store still holds the delta.

## Acceptance criteria

See `.adlc/specs/49-stock-graph.md` — each criterion names its verification. Summary: catalog completeness and validator survival (test/cli/stock-graph.test.ts); derived dependency closure (test/cli/stock-deps.test.ts); transitive install, skip-if-bound, divergence warning, evolve-with-report, driven through the real CLI (test/cli/stock-install.test.ts); depth — org nests ShallowPerson and not follows, object-level over GraphQL (test/cli/stock-depth.test.ts); thread one-read gather and strike moderation at BOTH levels (test/cli/stock-thread.test.ts); two-store federation story (test/cli/stock-federation.test.ts); prop-list and edge-reading pin plus no-identity-fields doctrine (test/cli/stock-pin.test.ts). Frozen rails test/cli/stock.test.ts and test/cli/pack-stock.test.ts stay untouched (T85); all new rails go in new files.

## Constraints

- rhizomatic is frozen. Expands-with-readings and the JSON term dialect exist since 0.8; no substrate change is needed. If one turns out to be needed, stop and surface it.
- §42.1 invariant: every entry stays a verbatim `loam register` file through the shared validator. No privileged path.
- Landing writes spec/49-stock-graph.md with provenance, amends §42.5's editorial-content paragraph, archives this ticket, and adds a capabilities-book chapter claim (test/site/capabilities.test.ts).
- Rails are declared at P3 when the test files exist, not before.
title: The stock graph — expand the shelf into an interconnected standard library with derived dependencies and transitive install
